scope: Ten-second matched real-scene MiniMax-H3 action-control comparison for insert-flower, handover-flower, and inspect-flower
summary: The stateful two-window pipeline produced three exact 10-second videos whose macro actions pass the pairwise distinctness proxy, but all six strict window evaluations reject identity, exact action/EPL, and flower-lock quality, and the overlap review exposes visible pose resets. The comparison is publishable only as PARTIAL evidence, not accepted long-horizon embodied control.
evidence: The typed long-horizon compiler produces exactly 240 camera-frame controls at 24 FPS and two legal 124-frame H3 windows with an eight-frame overlap; each action carries explicit object-holder transitions and its own frame-116 continuation reference.

Physical A800 GPU 3 completed six 832x480 H3 NF4 outputs using seed 20260811 and 20 steps; both immutable experiment metadata files record the selected physical GPU, CUDA/PyTorch runtime, commands, hashes, and three completed actions.

The packaged comparison and all three individual outputs decode to exactly 240 frames / 10.0 seconds. Pairwise full-frame MAD is 9.133966 for insert/handover, 9.600655 for insert/inspect, and 4.901000 for handover/inspect, above the declared 2.0 distinctness proxy.

All six strict window evaluations are rejected. Robot identity spans 0.673002-0.703279, motion preservation 0.166700-0.571315, EPL minimum 0.166700-0.552389, and flower lock 0.000481-0.000571; none establishes exact action execution or object contact.

The minimum-cost seam is frame 117 for all actions, with best-seam subject MAD 15.006603 for insert, 5.782332 for handover, and 9.282116 for inspect. Dense frame review confirms a visible pose reset near 4.9 seconds, especially for insert.

The replicated learned repair router enforces its non-regression contract. It selects bounded background repair when safe and retains the raw second-window insert candidate when every repair exceeds the declared motion/EPL regression tolerance.

The reusable agentic_skills/acwm-long-action-control skill passes skill-creator validation and the available offline SkillHone static check; repository tests passed 358 with one optional MuJoCo skip before the GPU run.
lessons: Per-action RGB continuation is sufficient to improve macro-action separation but not sufficient to carry diffusion state, precise robot pose, grasp state, or contact across a long-video boundary.
Pairwise visual distinctness and exact embodied action acceptance must remain separate gates: the three actions can look different while all six task evaluations still fail.
A learned repair router should expose an unrepairable world-model candidate rather than sacrifice action fidelity to manufacture a clean background score.
limitations: MiniMax-H3 uses third-party NF4 weights and two overlapping generation windows rather than one native 10-second diffusion trajectory.
The scene is a recorded real-world observation; the outputs are generated visualizations without calibrated forces, robot-base actions, persistent object state, or real-robot execution.
Human review remains pending, and the observed seam, grasp causality, flower identity, release, and contact physics are not accepted.

Full SkillHone model-graded evaluation was not run because the local SkillHone settings/provider file is absent; only skill validation, offline static checks, unit tests, and the real H3 forward campaign were available.
next_actions: Train a continuation-state adapter on matched overlap clips with explicit robot pose, object-holder, and flower-instance supervision rather than relying on one RGB reference frame.
Add a seam acceptance threshold and reject or regenerate any following window whose overlap subject MAD exceeds the calibrated bound before packaging.
Collect calibrated real-robot demonstrations with synchronized camera, joint/EEF state, contact, and persistent object identity before claiming embodied task control.
